Core distinction

Wide or long describes how a metric is stored. Additive or non-additive describes how it behaves. A long table may contain revenue, customer counts, prices, and conversion rates—each needs its own aggregation rule.

Implementation boundary

LookML cannot reconstruct information the source never retained.

Stored location-level distinct counts cannot produce an exact regional distinct count. Preserve entity identities, use a suitable mergeable sketch, or materialize the correct higher-grain value. The catalog marks these boundaries instead of hiding them behind syntax.
